messages:
Lina (CS): Escalating StayFit — dedicated cluster (dedicated-nyc1) hit widespread 429s during their 09:12 UTC hourly spike. Customer says requests started failing for ~90-120s before scale finished. min_replicas=1, max_replicas=10, burst_policy=standard. They’re pretty upset, asking for root cause and mitigation.
Ajay (Support): Ack. Do we have their RPS curve and autoscaler events? Any obvious throttles (auth/billing) in logs?
Lina (CS): Customer provided a small sample and timeline: baseline ~5 RPS, spike to ~160 RPS. They showed repeated 429 payloads and a few attach errors. Uploading their sample trace now.
Marco (SRE): Looking at control-plane events — autoscaler calculated scale but new pods stayed Pending. Early signs point to image pull/auth churn + slow node boot. Snip from controller events:
```
Autoscaler: ScaleUp request -> desired=8
kubelet: Pulling image "registry.redwood-internal/stayfit-runtime:stable"
imagepuller: manifest fetch 401 -> token refresh
kube-scheduler: PodPending -> no nodes registered
```
Marco (SRE): Also found cloud provider events showing nodes entering Provisioning then NotReady for ~30s due to cloud-init userdata + containerd start. So net time between scale decision and pod Ready was ~80-110s which matches customer timeline.
autoscale-bot: ALERT: scale_request(1751123460) desired=8 created=6 ready=1 duration=1m20s
Ajay (Support): So autoscaler wasn't the only bottleneck — node attach and image auth slowed things down. Any billing/quotas blocking image pulls?
Marco (SRE): No billing block. The registry token rotation coincided with spike which caused a few 401s and retries; image pull retried with backoff. Combined with new node boot latency, that amplified time-to-ready.
Priya (Eng Platform): Short-term mitigation we can push to customer: increase min_replicas to 3 during predicted spike window or enable prewarmed standby replicas (reserve 2). Medium-term: we should add staggered image prefetch on new nodes and make autoscaler factor in expected node-boot latency for that host pool.
Lina (CS): Customer prefers a config change they can apply immediately. I'll propose min_replicas=3 for peak hours and enable burst_reserved=2 if available. Want to confirm command to update their route.
Ajay (Support): Use the CLI: `redwood cli update --org stayfit --route their-route --min-replicas 3 --burst-reserve 2` — cross-check with Priya.
Priya (Eng Platform): That looks right. Also a lighter-weight workaround: set model variant fallback so some traffic served by cheaper warmdedicated nodes while new pods catch up.
Marco (SRE): Logging & repro steps I ran to validate:
1) replayed their spike with vegeta to 160 RPS for 90s against their dedicated endpoint
2) watched events: autoscaler requests nodes, cloud provider spins nodes, image pull 401s during token rotation, pods stuck Pending ~70-120s
Commands:
```
vegeta attack -duration=90s -rate=160 -targets=targets.txt | vegeta report
kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp -n stayfit
kubectl describe pod <pending-pod>
```
Marco (SRE): Repro reliably when I force token rotation during a spike. Without token churn new nodes come Ready in ~30s and scale feels fine.
Lina (CS): Great repro. I'll send customer the config change and explain root cause (concurrent image auth rotation + cold node boot). Any immediate ops we should run now?
Priya (Eng Platform): Ops: temporarily bump min_replicas to 3, enable burst reserve 2, and schedule a postmortem with engineering to harden new-node prefetch and make autoscaler consider worst-case boot+auth time. I'll make a ticket: ENGPLAT-5234.
autoscale-bot: Ticket created ENGPLAT-5234: "Pre-warm image cache & adjust autoscaler boot-time assumptions" assigned to @Priya.
Ajay (Support): I'll update StayFit and confirm when they apply change. If they need us to flip it, support can apply with their permission.
Lina (CS): Customer approved support apply. Ajay, please perform change and monitor for next hourly spike. I'll keep CS looped. :thumbsup:
Marco (SRE): I'll follow up with logs collection guide so we can triage faster next time (cloud-init timings + image pull metrics).
notes: thread is an incident-style escalation; root cause summary: image auth rotation + cold node boot increased scale latency. Recommended mitigations: bump min_replicas, reserve burst replicas, prefetch images and adjust autoscaler heuristics.
